chunks: My father and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-‘Aṭṭār, from Ḥamdān ibn Sulaymān al-Naysābūri, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Muḥammad al-Yamānī, from Manī‘ ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from Yūnus, from Ṣafwān al-Jammāl, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever performs Ghusl with the water of the Euphrates and visits the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), becomes like the day his mother gave birth to him, free of sins, even if he had committed major sins.
And they used to love the man who, when visiting the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), would perform Ghusl.
And when bidding farewell, he would not perform Ghusl, but would wipe his hand over his face when bidding farewell.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of performing Ghusl with Euphrates water before visiting Imam Husayn's grave?
ai.summary: This narration from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* underscores the profound spiritual purification associated with the Euphrates River, a key geographical and symbolic landmark in Shia pilgrimage geography, linking the physical act of Ghusl to the metaphysical cleansing of major sins. The companions' preference for pre-visit purification reflects a scholarly understanding of entering the sacred presence of Imam al-Ḥusayn (a.s.) in a state of ritual purity, while the post-visit hand-wiping signifies retaining the spiritual blessings (barakah) of the visitation. This practice highlights the Shia emphasis on the interconnection between physical geography, ritual hygiene, and devotional etiquette in honoring the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 1. My father and all of my scholars narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā Al-‘Aťťār, from Ḥamdān ibn Sulaymān Al-Naysābūri, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Muḥammad Al-Yamāni, from Manī’ ibn Ḥajjāj, from Yūnus, from Safwān Al-Jammāl, who said:

Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said: Those who perform Ghusl with the water of the Euphrates (River) and then go to the Ziyārah of the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.) become sinless like the day their mothers gave birth to them, even if they had committed major sins.
It is recommended that one performs Ghusl before going to the Ziyārah of the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.)
and not when bidding farewell (to him), but rather wipe one’s hands over the face when bidding farewell.
